audit_findings.title: FY2025 anchor may capitalize a project revenue peak
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 project revenue concentration was approximately $87.9m (13% of $676.368m); project-specific profit effect unquantified; FY2026 nine-month operating income declined $25.667m year over year
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring project contribution embedded in the $68.5m OE anchor is compounded through forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The project is valued at over $100 million in revenue, with equipment deliveries occurring throughout fiscal 2025 and continuing into the first quarter of fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The potential normalization error is not demonstrated because project-level profit was not disclosed, and a new MENA contract exceeding $80m partly supports continuing project revenue. Nevertheless, the original project completed in fiscal Q1 2026, results remain dependent on large irregular contracts, and nine-month operating income fell 33%. A meaningful project-profit adjustment could materially lower every scenario.
audit_findings.action: Obtain project-level gross profit, incremental operating costs and working capital for both MENA contracts; derive normalized OE excluding nonrecurring project economics and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Planned capital intensity may exceed the maintenance charge embedded in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 capex was $42.496m versus $20.896m depreciation and amortization, a $21.600m difference equal to 31.5% of anchor OE; FY2026 forecast capex is $50m-$55m; maintenance component unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Understated maintenance capex directly overstates annual OE and therefore operating PV and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Capital expenditures for fiscal 2026 are expected to range from approximately $50 million to $55 million, including equipment replacement, productivity improvements, new product development and commercial growth investments.
audit_findings.explanation: No demonstrated error exists because the record does not disclose the maintenance deduction used in the $68.5m anchor or separate replacement spending from discretionary growth and productivity investment. The disclosed spending scale is nevertheless large enough relative to anchor OE to be material if a recurring portion was omitted.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile anchor OE capex to the fixed-asset register and fiscal 2025-2026 projects, classify replacement, compliance, modernization and growth spending, estimate steady-state maintenance capex, and rerun the valuation with that charge.

audit_findings.title: Derivative liability bypasses earnings and is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.739m latest-quarter derivative liability, equal to approximately $1.21 per diluted share and 1.1% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: If the hedge liability is a separate nonoperating cash claim, omitting it from the bridge overstates equity value; its OCI treatment keeps the fair-value change outside OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Changes in the fair value of these contracts are reported in accumulated other comprehensive loss on the consolidated balance sheets and the fair value of these contracts is recorded within other noncurrent assets and other noncurrent liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing confirms the liability and its absence from the stated bridge, but a valuation error is not yet demonstrated because the swaps hedge foreign operating investments whose offsetting currency value may already be captured. The possible $1.21-per-share adjustment exceeds the $0.77 gap between bull value and market price, making bridge classification material.
audit_findings.action: Map each hedge to the foreign net investment, determine settlement cash obligations, tax, collateral and netting, test whether the offsetting foreign value is captured in operating PV, and rerun the bridge if the liability is incremental.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat operating cash as entirely excess
audit_findings.magnitude: $154.760m bridge exposure, equal to approximately $14.71 per diluted share and 13.9% of base equity value; required operating-cash amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash required for working capital, capital expenditures or project execution is an operating asset and should not be added to equity value as excess cash.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company requires cash for financing its receivables and inventories, paying operating expenses and capital expenditures, and for dividends and share repurchases.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge demonstrably adds the entire latest cash balance, while the filing states cash supports receivables, inventories, expenses and capital spending. The record does not establish how much is trapped or operationally required, so the amount of overstatement is unresolved, but even a moderate exclusion could materially change per-share values and the buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.action: Calculate minimum cash using monthly seasonal balances, working-capital peaks, committed capex, project guarantees, foreign accessibility and available credit; add only verified excess cash and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Unaccrued litigation could create a claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Uninsured judgments, settlements, deductibles and defense costs would reduce OE when incurred or create a liability deductible in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: While it is reasonably possible that a loss may be incurred, the Company is unable to estimate a range of potential loss due to the complexity and current status of these lawsuits.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing continues to classify loss as reasonably possible while stating that no range can be estimated and no accrual is recorded. This is a current unresolved contingency, not a demonstrated valuation error. Insurance and management's expectation reduce but do not eliminate the exposure; the record cannot establish whether it is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain subsequent docket developments, claim amounts, defense-cost history, policy limits, exclusions, deductibles, indemnities and any updated loss range; quantify and rerun OE or the bridge if a probable or decision-relevant exposure emerges.

audit_findings.title: Pessl equity-method earnings and stake value may be treated inconsistently
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.4m FY2025 equity-method income, 0.6% of anchor OE; $8.423m latest carrying value, approximately $0.80 per diluted share and 0.75% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method income enters OE while an alternatively separated stake value would enter the bridge; inconsistent use can double count earnings or omit net stake value.
audit_findings.evidence: Revenue and expenses of this investment are not consolidated into the Company’s financial statements; rather, the proportionate share of the earnings or losses is recorded within other income (expense), net on the consolidated statements of earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: Treatment consistency should be corrected, but the filed amounts are too small to alter the central conclusion. Even adding the entire $8.423m carrying value without removing embedded earnings would raise base value only from $106.17 to about $106.97 per share, still well below the $123.39 price; consistent treatment would produce a smaller net adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Trace distributions and the $0.4m income through OE, estimate investee maintenance needs, value the stake and call option, then either retain normalized distributable earnings in OE or remove them and add the stake separately.
